description:
Screen and, only from matched evidence, retain a SHA-addressed compiler wrapper that applies opt-level 1 to the ordinary `jit` library and CLI binary while leaving every test harness, dependency, server artifact, and direct developer Cargo invocation at opt-level 0.

## Background

Global and package-scoped test-profile optimization both met runtime goals but were rejected because they optimized all twelve `jit` test executables and nearly doubled representative rebuild cost. Most integration work instead links the ordinary `jit` library or launches the ordinary CLI. Cargo has no per-target profile override, but `RUSTC_WORKSPACE_WRAPPER` is fingerprinted and sees the exact rustc invocation, allowing a narrow, auditable experiment that excludes every `--test` harness. This compiler execution hook is supply-chain-sensitive and must fail closed rather than rely on mutable environment behavior.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A tracked, shell-safe wrapper adds exactly one trailing `-C opt-level=1` only when package and crate identities are `jit`, the canonical crate root is `crates/jit/src/lib.rs` or `crates/jit/src/main.rs`, and `--test` is absent; every harness, integration crate, `jit-server`, dependency, build script, compiler probe, unknown shape, exit status, signal, stdout, and stderr passes through unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-02: Cargo uses an ordinary, SHA-256-addressed staged wrapper path so wrapper-content changes invalidate fingerprints; the gate refuses an unexpected preexisting workspace wrapper, never evaluates arguments, preserves line-table backtraces, and scopes the wrapper only to test-build, nextest, doctest, provenance, and budget commands while formatting and clippy retain their existing compiler boundary.
- [hard] REQ-03: An audit record from a real candidate no-run proves every and only eligible ordinary `jit` library and binary invocation received opt-level 1, no invocation already carried a conflicting optimization level, and no test harness, server, dependency, build script, or probe was modified.
- [hard] REQ-04: A fixed-revision one-sample screen compares fresh isolated opt-level-0 and candidate targets under identical 24-worker, no-sccache, incremental-disabled conditions; it rejects before retention for any classification, fingerprint, correctness, identity, line-table, active-byte, target-size, resource, build, or representative rebuild failure, including clean or comment-touch build regression above 25 percent.
- [hard] REQ-05: One passing screen authorizes, but does not replace, three matched clean-build, representative-rebuild, already-built nextest, and doctest samples. Retention requires exact runnable, ignored, and doctest identity sets, all assertions passing, median aggregate test-work reduction of at least 200 seconds, every nextest sample at or below 23,500 milliseconds with no test above 20 seconds, doctests at or below 5,500 milliseconds, active test executables below two gibibytes, target size below ten gibibytes, and a green authoritative cargo-ci. Otherwise the wrapper integration is reverted and complete `no_change` evidence is recorded.

## Notes

Do not set a global test-profile optimization, optimize test harnesses, overwrite `target/debug/jit`, or prebuild outside the named suite clock. Direct ordinary Cargo remains unchanged. Prove sccache nesting before retaining it, or explicitly disable and measure sccache only for wrapper-covered commands.
title: Screen ordinary JIT artifacts with a compiler wrapper
